studioRows.protection: spendable only with the key NFT; in other wallets a nameless NFT, so keep it.
studioRows.protectionHelp: The key NFT is what Studio calls an AuthKey. It opens an AuthGuard, the contract Studio keeps the identity in, so the identity spends only with the key, whichever app holds the seed. Other wallets show the key as a nameless NFT, which is how one gets sent away or burned; this wallet names it by what it guards.

freeze.title: Freeze this UTXO

A frozen UTXO stays in your wallet but is left out of every payment this app makes, so your spendable balance drops by {amount}. Unfreeze it from this list at any time.

Freezing only applies here: if you use this seed phrase in another wallet application, freeze the same UTXO there too.
freeze.messageToken:
A frozen UTXO stays in your wallet but is left out of every payment and token transfer this app makes, so the tokens on it and the {amount} it holds cannot be spent from here. Unfreeze it from this list at any time.

Freezing only applies here: if you use this seed phrase in another wallet application, freeze the same UTXO there too.

warnings.notAPayment: A pledge is not a payment. The money only moves if the campaign reaches its target, and until then the UTXO is held back and not part of what you can spend.
warnings.dappActions: While a pledge is open, dApp actions from this wallet may fail, because the wallet will not sign away the pledged UTXO. Use a separate wallet for pledges if you use dApps regularly.
warnings.dappActionsDetail: This applies to WalletConnect and WizardConnect, where the dApp builds its own transaction and can pick the pledged UTXO. CashConnect is unaffected: the wallet picks the UTXOs there, and leaves the pledged one out.
warnings.otherDevices: The UTXO is only held back in this app. Do not spend from this wallet on another device or in other wallet software while a pledge is open, because that can cancel your pledge.
warnings.otherDevicesDetail: Another wallet has no way to know the UTXO is held back, so it may pick it for an ordinary payment. The campaign can then no longer use your signed pledge, and this wallet will only see that the UTXO is gone, not why. If you use this seed phrase in another wallet application, freeze or reserve the same UTXO there too, which most wallets support.

learn.title: Identities on Bitcoin Cash
learn.purpose: It is a way to publish information about something on Bitcoin Cash, its metadata, such as a token's name and icon. Anyone can verify that the information came from whoever controls the identity, and the controller can update it over time or pass control on.
learn.whatLead: Under the hood, an identity is a chain of transactions.
learn.what: It starts at the authbase, which for a token is the token id, and continues through each transaction that spends the previous one's output 0. The latest unspent output 0 is the identity UTXO: whoever holds it controls the identity, and moving it to a new address is the transfer.
learn.tokens: Its token id is the identity's id, which is how an issuer can update a token's name and icon after the tokens are out. Identities that are not tokens exist too: a person, an organization or a contract can publish information the same way.
learn.metadataLead: The metadata is a hosted file.
learn.metadata: A registry in the BCMR format is hosted off-chain, and a publication output on the chain commits to its hash, so anyone can fetch the file and check it against the chain. A token's registry is written with the {generator}; any registry can be written by hand against the {schema}.
learn.keysLead: AuthKeys are a CashTokens Studio convention.
learn.keys: {studio} keeps an identity's UTXO in a covenant, the AuthGuard, and turns the right to move it into an NFT, the AuthKey. This wallet recognises such keys, lists what they control and protects them like an identity UTXO.
learn.further: The {spec} describes identities, registries and publication in full.

create.label: Add a new identity that is not a token
create.help: The standard's identities are not only tokens: the same chain of UTXOs can stand for a dapp, a contract system or an organization, and prove who controls it.
create.helpNaming: One transaction makes it, and naming comes after, with a publication that names its id.
create.hint: A name, icon and links for a dapp, a contract system or an organization, published and updated from one UTXO with no token on it.
create.pick: Any UTXO at output 0 without a token can be an identity: its transaction id becomes the identity's permanent id. Its BCH stays held back with the identity for as long as it is held, so a small UTXO is best.
create.prepareMessage: This sends {amount} to yourself now, so the identity has a fresh UTXO at output 0. The amount stays yours; only the fee is spent.

steps.pick: pick the UTXO that becomes the identity's id

create.confirmTitle: Add this UTXO as an identity?
create.confirmMessage: {outpoint} becomes the identity's UTXO, held back from coin selection with its {amount}. Its transaction id becomes the identity's permanent id.
create.tokenPointer: Nearly every identity currently belongs to a token. To create a token identity, {link}: the transaction that creates the token creates its identity at the same time.
create.novelHelp: A dapp could say which version of its contracts is current and where its site is; an organization could stand behind what it publishes. Almost none exist yet and little reads them, so know what you want from one before making it.
create.lead: Will you write and host its registry yourself?
create.outcome: Adding lists the identity under the ones this wallet owns and keeps its UTXO out of ordinary sends. It has no name until a registry naming it is published, which its card walks you through.
create.registry: the JSON file that names the identity, written in a code editor against the {schema} and hosted on a domain you control or on IPFS.
create.registryNote: The {generator} writes registries for tokens: it asks for a symbol and writes a token section, which an identity that is not a token must not have. Its snapshot carries a name, a description and links.
